/-!
# Eilenberg–Ganea conjecture

The Eilenberg–Ganea conjecture states that if a group $G$ has cohomological dimension $2$, then it
has a $2$-dimensional Eilenberg–MacLane space $K(G, 1)$.

Here the cohomological dimension of $G$ is the integral one,
$$\operatorname{cd}(G) = \sup \{n : H^n(G, M) \neq 0 \text{ for some }
\mathbb{Z}G\text{-module } M\},$$
which is also the projective dimension of the trivial module $\mathbb{Z}$ over the integral group
ring $\mathbb{Z}G$. A $K(G, 1)$ is a path-connected CW complex whose fundamental group is
isomorphic to $G$ and whose higher homotopy groups $\pi_n$, $n \geq 2$, are all trivial.

For $n \neq 2$, a group of cohomological dimension $n$ always has an $n$-dimensional $K(G, 1)$, and
a group of cohomological dimension $2$ always has a $3$-dimensional $K(G, 1)$. Bestvina and Brady
showed that the Eilenberg–Ganea conjecture and the Whitehead asphericity conjecture cannot both be
true.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Eilenberg–Ganea conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eilenberg%E2%80%93Ganea_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [EG57] Eilenberg, Samuel; Ganea, Tudor. *On the Lusternik–Schnirelmann category of abstract
  groups*. Annals of Mathematics 65 (1957), 517–518. https://doi.org/10.2307/1970062
- [BB97] Bestvina, Mladen; Brady, Noel. *Morse theory and finiteness properties of groups*.
  Inventiones Mathematicae 129 (1997), 445–470. https://doi.org/10.1007/s002220050168
-/

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem cohomologicalDimension_eq_two_iff (G : Type) [Group G] :
    cohomologicalDimension G = 2 ↔
      (∃ A : Rep ℤ G, Nontrivial (groupCohomology A 2)) ∧
        ∀ n : ℕ, 2 < n → ∀ A : Rep ℤ G, Subsingleton (groupCohomology A n) := by
  simp only [← not_nontrivial_iff_subsingleton]
  unfold cohomologicalDimension
  set P : ℕ → Prop := fun n => ∃ A : Rep ℤ G, Nontrivial (groupCohomology A n) with hP
  constructor
  · intro h
    have hle : ∀ n, P n → (n : ℕ∞) ≤ 2 := fun n hn =>
      h ▸ le_iSup₂ (f := fun n (_ : P n) => (n : ℕ∞)) n hn
    refine ⟨?_, fun n hn A hA => ?_⟩
    · by_contra h2
      have : ⨆ n, ⨆ (_ : P n), (n : ℕ∞) ≤ 1 := by
        refine iSup₂_le fun n hn => ?_
        have := hle n hn
        have hn2 : n ≠ 2 := fun e => h2 (e ▸ hn)
        norm_cast at this ⊢
        omega
      rw [h] at this
      exact absurd this (by decide)
    · have := hle n ⟨A, hA⟩
      norm_cast at this
      omega
  · rintro ⟨h2, h⟩
    apply le_antisymm
    · refine iSup₂_le fun n hn => ?_
      by_contra hlt
      push_neg at hlt
      obtain ⟨A, hA⟩ := hn
      exact h n (by exact_mod_cast hlt) A hA
    · exact le_iSup₂ (f := fun n (_ : P n) => (n : ℕ∞)) 2 h2

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem cohomologicalDimension_eq_zero_of_subsingleton (G : Type) [Group G] [Subsingleton G] :
    cohomologicalDimension G = 0 := by
  refine le_antisymm (iSup₂_le fun n hn => ?_) (zero_le _)
  obtain ⟨A, hA⟩ := hn
  cases n with
  | zero => exact le_rfl
  | succ n =>
    have := ModuleCat.isZero_iff_subsingleton.1
      (isZero_groupCohomology_succ_of_subsingleton A n)
    exact absurd this (not_subsingleton_iff_nontrivial.2 hA)

blocks.docstring:
A topological space `X` is an Eilenberg–MacLane space `K(G, 1)` for the group `G` if it is
path-connected and, for every basepoint `x`, the fundamental group `π₁(X, x)` is isomorphic to `G`
and the higher homotopy groups `πₙ(X, x)`, `n ≥ 2`, are trivial. The CW complex condition that is
usually part of the definition of a `K(G, 1)` is imposed separately in the conjecture below.

justification.closest_existing_considered: FundamentalGroup, HomotopyGroup.Pi (π_), ContractibleSpace (universal-cover formulation not available).
justification.name: EilenbergGaneaConjecture.IsEilenbergMacLaneSpace
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no definition of Eilenberg–MacLane spaces. Defined as `PathConnectedSpace X ∧ ∀ x, Nonempty (FundamentalGroup X x ≃* G) ∧ ∀ n ≥ 2, Subsingleton (π_ n X x)`, i.e. π₀ trivial, π₁ ≅ G, πₙ = 0 for n ≥ 2, using Mathlib's FundamentalGroup and HomotopyGroup.Pi.

blocks.name: IsEilenbergMacLaneSpace
blocks.text:
/-- A topological space `X` is an Eilenberg–MacLane space `K(G, 1)` for the group `G` if it is
path-connected and, for every basepoint `x`, the fundamental group `π₁(X, x)` is isomorphic to `G`
and the higher homotopy groups `πₙ(X, x)`, `n ≥ 2`, are trivial. The CW complex condition that is
usually part of the definition of a `K(G, 1)` is imposed separately in the conjecture below. -/
def IsEilenbergMacLaneSpace (G : Type*) [Group G] (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop :=
  PathConnectedSpace X ∧
    ∀ x : X, Nonempty (FundamentalGroup X x ≃* G) ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n → Subsingleton (π_ n X x)

@[category test, AMS 55]
theorem isEilenbergMacLaneSpace_unit : IsEilenbergMacLaneSpace PUnit Unit := by
  refine ⟨inferInstance, fun _ => ⟨⟨?_⟩, fun n _ => ?_⟩⟩
  · haveI : Subsingleton (FundamentalGroup Unit ()) :=
      inferInstanceAs (Subsingleton (Path.Homotopic.Quotient (() : Unit) ()))
    haveI : Unique (FundamentalGroup Unit ()) := Unique.mk' _
    exact MulEquiv.ofUnique
  · exact Quotient.instSubsingletonQuotient _

@[category research open, AMS 20 55 57]
theorem eilenberg_ganea_conjecture (G : Type) [Group G] (hG : cohomologicalDimension G = 2) :
    ∃ (X : Type) (_ : TopologicalSpace X) (_ : T2Space X) (_ : CWComplex (univ : Set X)),
      (∀ n : ℕ, 2 < n → IsEmpty (cell (univ : Set X) n)) ∧
        Nonempty (cell (univ : Set X) 2) ∧
        IsEilenbergMacLaneSpace G X := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
**Eilenberg–Ganea conjecture** [EG57]: a group with cohomological dimension $2$ also has a
$2$-dimensional Eilenberg–MacLane space $K(G, 1)$.

That is, if $\operatorname{cd}(G) = 2$, then there is a Hausdorff space $X$ carrying a CW complex
structure of dimension $2$ (no cells of dimension greater than $2$, and at least one $2$-cell) which
is path-connected, has fundamental group isomorphic to $G$, and has trivial homotopy groups
$\pi_n(X)$ for all $n \geq 2$.

Since $\operatorname{cd}(G) = 2$ forces every $K(G, 1)$ to have dimension at least $2$, the
requirement that $X$ has a $2$-cell is automatic; it is included so that $X$ is literally
$2$-dimensional.

That is, if $\operatorname{cd}(G) = 2$, then there is a Hausdorff space $X$ carrying a CW complex

Since $\operatorname{cd}(G) = 2$ forces every $K(G, 1)$ to have dimension at least $2$, the

@[category research open, AMS 20 55 57]
theorem eilenberg_ganea_conjecture (G : Type) [Group G] (hG : cohomologicalDimension G = 2) :
    ∃ (X : Type) (_ : TopologicalSpace X) (_ : T2Space X) (_ : CWComplex (univ : Set X)),
      (∀ n : ℕ, 2 < n → IsEmpty (cell (univ : Set X) n)) ∧
        Nonempty (cell (univ : Set X) 2) ∧
        IsEilenbergMacLaneSpace G X := by
  sorry

claims.decomposer_note: Universally quantified over all (discrete) groups G: if the integral cohomological dimension cd_ℤ(G) equals 2 then there exists a 2-dimensional aspherical CW-complex with fundamental group G (i.e. geometric dimension gd(G) = 2); the reverse inequality cd ≤ gd is automatic, and the known facts that cd = gd for n ≠ 2, that cd = 2 implies gd ≤ 3, and the Bestvina–Brady 'not both EG and Whitehead' result are context only, not additional questions posed by the statement.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same implication (cd_ℤ(G) = 2 ⇒ ∃ 2-dimensional K(G,1)) and all compile; none is unfaithful in substance. c07 chosen as the base: its cohomological dimension is the textbook sup{n : Hⁿ(G,A) ≠ 0 for some ℤG-module A} built directly on Mathlib's `groupCohomology` over `Rep ℤ G`, and it comes with a proven API lemma (`cohomologicalDimension_eq_two_iff`) showing the ℕ∞-supremum encoding matches the elementary reading of 'cohomological dimension 2', plus a trivial-group test. Its conclusion is a Hausdorff (`T2Space`) Mathlib classical `CWComplex` on the whole space with no cells above dimension 2 and at least one 2-cell, path-connected, π₁ ≅ G at every basepoint, πₙ trivial for n ≥ 2. Edits: the K(G,1) conditions were factored into c01's named `IsEilenbergMacLaneSpace` predicate (∀-basepoint form, generalized to Type*) with c06's one-point-space test adapted to it; docstrings expanded. c03 and c05 were not used because they omit `T2Space` (Mathlib's `CWComplex` deliberately does not require Hausdorffness, so without it the conclusion is weaker than a genuine CW complex); c02/c08 are correct but inline everything with `@`-syntax and lack API/tests; c01/c04/c06 are equally faithful alternatives (projective-dimension or ¬IsZero encodings).
claims.source_text: a group with cohomological dimension 2 also has a 2-dimensional Eilenberg–MacLane space $K(G, 1)$

context:
The Eilenberg–Ganea conjecture is a claim in algebraic topology.  It was formulated by Samuel Eilenberg and Tudor Ganea in 1957, in a short but influential paper.  It states that if a group G has cohomological dimension 2, then it has a 2-dimensional Eilenberg–MacLane space $K(G,1)$.  For n different from 2, a group G of cohomological dimension n has an n-dimensional Eilenberg–MacLane space. It is also known that a group of cohomological dimension 2 has a 3-dimensional Eilenberg−MacLane space.
In 1997,  Mladen Bestvina and Noel Brady constructed a group G so that either G is a counterexample to the Eilenberg–Ganea conjecture, or there must be a counterexample to the Whitehead conjecture; in other words, it is not possible for both conjectures to be true.

decomposition_objections.text: None. The single slot is correct: the statement is one universally quantified implication (cd_ℤ(G) = 2 ⇒ there is a 2-dimensional K(G,1)), and the surrounding facts (cd = gd for n ≠ 2, cd = 2 ⇒ gd ≤ 3, Bestvina–Brady) are context only and are mentioned only in the module docstring.

$2$-dimensional Eilenberg–MacLane space $K(G, 1)$.

That is, if $\operatorname{cd}(G) = 2$, then there is a Hausdorff space $X$ carrying a CW complex
structure of dimension $2$ (no cells of dimension greater than $2$, and at least one $2$-cell) which
is path-connected, has fundamental group isomorphic to $G$, and has trivial homotopy groups
$\pi_n(X)$ for all $n \geq 2$.

Since $\operatorname{cd}(G) = 2$ forces every $K(G, 1)$ to have dimension at least $2$, the
requirement that $X$ has a $2$-cell is automatic; it is included so that $X$ is literally
$2$-dimensional. -/
@[category research open, AMS 20 55 57]
theorem eilenberg_ganea_conjecture (G : Type) [Group G] (hG : cohomologicalDimension G = 2) :
    ∃ (X : Type) (_ : TopologicalSpace X) (_ : T2Space X) (_ : CWComplex (univ : Set X)),
      (∀ n : ℕ, 2 < n → IsEmpty (cell (univ : Set X) n)) ∧
        Nonempty (cell (univ : Set X) 2) ∧
        IsEilenbergMacLaneSpace G X := by
  sorry

end EilenbergGaneaConjecture

items: Cohomological dimension is the integral one (ℤ coefficients), as the decomposition notes require: cohomologicalDimension G := ⨆ (n : ℕ) (_ : ∃ A : Rep ℤ G, Nontrivial (groupCohomology A n)), (n : ℕ∞). Mathlib's groupCohomology A n is isomorphic to Ext^n(ℤ, A) in Rep ℤ G (groupCohomologyIsoExt), so this is the textbook sup{n : H^n(G,M) ≠ 0 for some ℤG-module M}. The file proves cohomologicalDimension G = 2 ↔ (∃ A, H^2(G,A) ≠ 0) ∧ ∀ n > 2, ∀ A, H^n(G,A) = 0, so the ℕ∞-supremum encoding provably matches the elementary reading; the sSup ∅ = 0 default is unreachable anyway since H^0(G,ℤ) = ℤ ≠ 0.

G : Type (universe 0) rather than Type*: Rep ℤ G requires k and G in the same universe as ℤ : Type. ℤG-modules quantified over are those in universe 0, which suffices to detect cd (the relevant test modules are syzygies of a free resolution in the same universe as G).

'2-dimensional Eilenberg–MacLane space K(G,1)' is modeled topologically: ∃ (X : Type) with a TopologicalSpace, T2Space, and Mathlib classical CW structure CWComplex (univ : Set X); PathConnectedSpace X; for every basepoint x, Nonempty (FundamentalGroup X x ≃* G) and Subsingleton (π_ n X x) for all n ≥ 2. Quantifying over every basepoint is equivalent to quantifying over one because X is path-connected.

Dimension exactly 2 is encoded literally: (∀ n > 2, IsEmpty (cell univ n)) ∧ Nonempty (cell univ 2). Under the hypothesis cd G = 2 this is equivalent to 'dimension ≤ 2' (gd ≤ 2), because cd G ≤ gd G always; the exact-dimension form matches the wording '2-dimensional' and the notes' 'gd(G) = 2'.

T2Space X is assumed explicitly because Mathlib's Topology.CWComplex class deliberately does not require the ambient space to be Hausdorff, whereas the classical (Whitehead/Hatcher) definition of a CW complex does; with T2 the Mathlib structure is a genuine CW complex on X.
The CW structure is placed on the whole space (C = Set.univ) so that the homotopy groups of X itself are the homotopy groups of the complex; this loses no generality.
X : Type (universe 0), matching G : Type and existing repo idioms (∃ (X : Type) (_ : TopologicalSpace X), …).

Two auxiliary provable declarations were added for the bespoke definition per CONTRIBUTING's 'add basic API tests': cohomologicalDimension_eq_two_iff (category API) and cohomologicalDimension_eq_zero_of_subsingleton (category test); neither uses sorry.

reviewer_notes: Interpretation choices (all standard, documented in docstrings): (1) cohomological dimension is the integral one cd_ℤ(G), defined as ⨆ n with ∃ A : Rep ℤ G, Hⁿ(G,A) nontrivial, in ℕ∞; the sup over the empty set never arises since H⁰(G,ℤ) ≠ 0. Equivalent to projectiveDimension (Rep.trivial ℤ G ℤ) used by c01/c02/c03/c08 via Mathlib's groupCohomologyIsoExt, but that equivalence is not proven in Mathlib in a directly usable form, so the elementary definition was preferred. (2) G : Type (universe 0) is forced by Mathlib's `Rep k G` same-universe requirement; this is the repo idiom (cf. SurjunctiveGroup, GapConjecture, Kaplansky) and not a mathematical restriction. (3) '2-dimensional' is encoded literally as exact CW dimension 2 (some 2-cell, no cells of dimension > 2); under cd(G) = 2 this is equivalent to the usual gd(G) ≤ 2 formulation since a 1-dimensional aspherical CW complex has free fundamental group (cd ≤ 1). (4) T2Space is required explicitly because Mathlib's `Topology.CWComplex` omits Hausdorffness while classical CW complexes are Hausdorff; genuine K(G,1) CW complexes always satisfy it. (5) Basepoint quantified universally; equivalent to existential by path-connectedness. The context facts (cd = gd for n ≠ 2, cd = 2 ⇒ gd ≤ 3, Bestvina–Brady) are mentioned only in the module docstring, as the decomposition table prescribes. Final file compiles with only the `declaration uses 'sorry'` warning; two URL lines in the module docstring exceed 100 characters, as is common in existing repo files.
statement: Eilenberg–Ganea conjecture: a group with cohomological dimension 2 also has a 2-dimensional Eilenberg–MacLane space $K(G, 1)$.
